descriptionChirho: A state of tranquility, harmony, and well-being -- encompassing interpersonal reconciliation, inner spiritual rest, and the messianic peace of God's kingdom. This is the Greek counterpart of Hebrew 'shalom', used extensively across the NT in greetings, blessings, and theological discourse (Matt 10:13, 10:34; Mark 5:34; Luke 1:79, 2:14, 2:29; John 14:27, 16:33, 20:19; Rom 1:7, 5:1, 8:6, 14:17; Gal 5:22; Eph 2:14-17; Phil 4:7; Col 3:15). All translations converge on one concept: Spanish 'paz/de paz', Hindi 'shanti' (शान्ति/शान्ति का), Arabic 'salamun/salamin' (سَلامٌ/سَلامٍ), Korean 'pyeonghwa' (평화가/평화의), Swahili 'amani/wa amani/ya amani'. S66429 is simply the genitive case ('of peace') of the same noun, not a distinct lexical meaning.
